name: gizza-ai/fiscal-quarter-mapper
summary: Label a CSV date column with fiscal quarters and fiscal years

tool.description: Append fiscal-quarter and fiscal-year label columns to a CSV/TSV table whose date column can start its fiscal year in any month (january = calendar, april = UK/India, july = Australia, october = US federal). The fiscal year can be named by the calendar year it ends in (US federal / pandas) or the one it begins in (the common spreadsheet recipe), and labels render as Q1 FY2026, FY2026-Q1, 2026-Q1, 2026Q1, Q1, or 1. Optional columns add the quarter's start and end dates, the fiscal month 1-12, and the row's day-of-quarter out of days-in-quarter. It reads ISO, US, European, written-month, compact YYYYMMDD, month-precision and timestamped values, settles ambiguous DD/MM vs MM/DD column-wide from rows that can only be read one way, and can blank, drop, or raise on unreadable cells. Output is the rewritten CSV, a plain-text audit report, or JSON carrying both.

add_fiscal_month.description: Append a fiscal_month column numbered 1-12 from the fiscal start month (october start: October = 1). Default false.

add_fiscal_year.description: Append a fiscal_year column next to fiscal_quarter. Default true.

add_quarter_dates.description: Append fiscal_quarter_start and fiscal_quarter_end columns as ISO YYYY-MM-DD dates. Default false.

add_quarter_position.description: Append day_of_quarter and days_in_quarter columns, measured from the row's own date (quarters run 90-92 days). Default false.

column.description: Which column holds the dates: a header name ("closed"), a 0-based index ("1"), or "auto" (default) to pick the first column where at least 60% of non-blank cells parse as a date. With header=false only an index works.

date_order.description: How to read an all-numeric value like 03/04/2024. "auto" (default) settles the whole column from rows that can only be read one way (a day above 12) and falls back to month-first; day-first forces DD/MM/YYYY; month-first forces MM/DD/YYYY. ISO YYYY-MM-DD is unaffected.

delimiter.description: Input/output delimiter. auto (default) sniffs comma, tab, semicolon, or pipe from the first non-blank line; choose one to force it. The output uses the same delimiter as the input.

fiscal_start_month.description: Calendar month the fiscal year starts in. january = calendar year (default), april = UK/India, july = Australia/NZ, october = US federal.

fiscal_year_label.description: Format of the fiscal_year column (and of the year embedded in q-fy/fy-q quarter labels): fy-yyyy = "FY2026" (default), yyyy = "2026", fy-yy = "FY26", range = "2025-2026", range-short = "2025-26". Ranges collapse to one year when the fiscal year starts in january.

fiscal_year_naming.description: Which calendar year names the fiscal year. "end" (default) matches the US federal government and pandas: Oct 2025 is FY2026. "start" matches the common spreadsheet recipe: Oct 2025 is FY2025. The two conventions differ by one, so pick deliberately.

header.description: Treat the first row as column names. Default true. Turn off for a bare list of dates with no header row.

input.description: CSV/TSV text with a date column, e.g. "invoice,closed\nA-1,2025-10-14". Include the header row when header=true. Capped at 5,000,000 bytes.

on_error.description: What to do with a cell that cannot be read as a date: blank (default) leaves the added columns empty, drop removes the row, error stops and names the offending row and line.

output.description: csv (default) returns the input with the fiscal columns appended; report returns a plain-text audit (column picked, date order and the evidence for it, rows per quarter, unreadable values); json returns that audit plus the CSV as a JSON object.

quarter_label.description: Format of the fiscal_quarter column: q-fy = "Q1 FY2026" (default), fy-q = "FY2026-Q1", yyyy-qn = "2026-Q1", yyyyqn = "2026Q1" (pandas style), qn = "Q1", n = "1".
